title: fix: keep shell snapshot capture from freezing the gateway
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Capturing a shell snapshot before a host command could freeze the entire Gateway for several seconds while btrfs committed a transaction. Exec preparation and a detached upload-cleanup timer also lacked task names in main-thread stall reports.

## User Impact

Shell snapshot capture now creates its temporary directory and output file asynchronously, so those filesystem operations no longer block the Gateway event loop. Remaining preparation or upload-cleanup stalls have structural task names. No configuration, protocol, dependency, or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Production kernel samples showed 6.3-second and 7.9-second main-thread freezes in `D / wait_current_trans / syscall 437` (`openat2`); one overlapped a 13.5-second btrfs commit and had no CPU profile. Subsequent tracing identified `.` followed by `openclaw-shell-snapshot-<uuid>-<rand>` as the main-thread opens. The async fs-safe temp-workspace API synchronously creates its native root and exclusive file, identifying shell snapshot capture as the owner.

Use async `node:fs/promises` at that owner: `mkdtemp` creates a fresh private directory, directory permissions are 0700, and the output opens with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` and 0600 permissions. Capture reads the retained descriptor and closes it before recursive cleanup in `finally`, including failure exits. The existing capture subprocess still writes its output inside that private directory. This removes the fs-safe temp-workspace path without adding a worker or changing fs-safe; the existing trusted temp-root resolver remains responsible for root admission.

Exec preparation runs under `exec:spawn-prepare`; detached upload expiration runs under `terminal-upload:cleanup`, both using the existing stall-attribution owner. No path contents or user data enter either label.

## Evidence

The owner regression failed on the base for both successful capture and shell failure: no async output open was observed (`expected [] to have a length of 1`). It now passes through real shell capture with private-directory permissions, exclusive/no-follow creation, cleanup on failure, and an injected symlink collision that leaves its target untouched. Existing shell behavior, cache, subprocess and broker-deadline suites pass. The Node-specific exec-entrypoint test records a simulated 1,200 ms resumed preparation stall as `exec:spawn-prepare`; the existing upload-expiry test checks its detached callback's task name.

Focused validation passed:

- Shell snapshot, cache, spawn, broker, exec-host-spawn and terminal-upload run: 33 passed, one Bun-only skip; that skipped V8 continuation test subsequently passed on Node. The snapshot environment-worker and exec-host-gateway suites also passed in the initial run.
- Node stall-attribution, stall flight-recorder, exec-host-spawn and fs-safe wrapper run: 163 passed, six platform skips. Remaining fs-safe environment and stall-observer run: 15 passed, one platform skip.
- Core typecheck (`run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`), changed test graphs (`agents-root`, `agents-tools`, `infra`), targeted oxlint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated Codex autoreview of the complete local change against base `42731417524048fccefad9be332dc134173bd6b7`, through P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. `pr-simplify` retained the direct owner fix and existing task mechanism; no new machinery.

The first terminal-test attempt exposed an extra timer created by its new monitor fixture; removing unnecessary heartbeat sampling restored the existing one-timer invariant. The initial test typecheck caught an optional `fs.open` argument type in the observation record; it now uses the actual API parameter types. Both checks pass after those test-only corrections. Tests remain bounded: the three new real-filesystem capture cases took 51/9/10 ms in the focused run; the existing broker deadline proof retains its existing six-second wait. No production access or btrfs contention reproduction was performed; Linux-native contention remains production evidence, with broad cross-platform proof delegated to PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Remaining filesystem candidates and follow-ups</summary>

The confirmed snapshot caller runs on a cache miss or refresh (five-minute freshness per shell/cwd/environment key), rather than every command. The detached upload timer runs at the earliest retained expiry, with hourly error retries; it is now attributed, while its shared cleanup lock remains unchanged.

The audit found these other create/mutate paths. Absolute event rates are unavailable, so workload-dependent candidates cannot be ranked by measured frequency:

- `src/infra/terminal-file-upload.ts:114` timer and `:138` cleanup-lock acquisition: confirmed detached main-thread route; task attribution fixed here. Moving the shared lock requires preserving its cross-process recovery semantics.
- `src/plugin-sdk/file-lock.ts:166`: generic fs-safe sidecar acquisition, per lock acquisition; the promise-returning API reaches synchronous native exclusive create when no lock root is supplied.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-profile-lock.ts:16`: per OAuth profile mutation/refresh, via the shared lock owner. No separate detached recurring entry was established in this audit.
- `src/plugins/provider-auth-persistence.ts:255`: one lock per persistence target, via the same owner; entry context depends on the auth flow.
- `src/config/write-lock.ts:197`, `:301`, `:341`: config/source lock acquisition and contention, per config mutation. Reentrancy, stale recovery, borrowed-resource guards, and multiple source locks make this a separate owner-level change.
- `src/media/store.ts:275`, `:549`; `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.ts:164`; `src/storage/filesystem.ts:80`, `:105`: per artifact/media write; native parent creation/admission can be synchronous inside these async methods. An untracked entry was not established.
- `src/infra/package-lifecycle.ts:169`: per lifecycle operation; rooted and unrooted lock paths differ. No recurring untracked entry was established.
- `src/config/source-file-stability.ts:24`, `:38` via `src/infra/fs-observation-snapshot.ts:16`: 50 ms metadata polling while a config file settles, a read-stall candidate rather than a confirmed exclusive-create route. The primary watcher already carries a task scope.

These are follow-ups, not additional identified incident owners. Shared lock behavior was not replaced speculatively.
</details>
